c.v: Commercial metal roofing

runs.v: is a roof covering of formed metal panels — steel, aluminum, or copper — fitted as concealed-fastener standing-seam or exposed-fastener systems on large-span commercial roofs. The metal panels carry long-span low- and steep-slope roofs across a multi-decade ownership horizon.

For owners and property managers weighing commercial metal roofing Newark NJ options, the case is longevity: metal roofing systems last 40 to 80 years depending on the type and with proper maintenance, and a durable metal roof is fully recyclable and sustainable at the end of that life.

sections.heading: Metal vs. TPO, EPDM, PVC, and Built-Up Roofing for Low-Slope Commercial Roofing Needs

c.v: The initial cost of metal roofing may be higher, but it lowers long-term costs due to its durability.

runs.v: TPO roofing lasts 7 to 20 years, EPDM roofing 15 to 25 years, and built-up roofing can last over 30 years with proper care; PVC roofing is known for its high UV resistance and durability. Metal roofs reflect solar radiant heat, reducing cooling costs: reflective metal surfaces can lower summer cooling bills by up to 25 percent, so metal roofing is energy-efficient and minimizes heat absorption.

Metal roofing provides excellent fire resistance and often carries a Class A fire rating, and it offers exceptional durability and weather resistance, withstanding heavy rain, snowstorms, and gale-force winds when properly installed. Options include standing seam, corrugated panels, and metal shingles; commercial buildings mostly use standing-seam or ribbed panels.

sections.heading: Our Commercial Metal Roofing Process, Step by Step

items.v: Engineering and Panel Selection

A Newark Quality Roofing technician assesses the building, the wind exposure, and the existing roof, then specifies the panel profile, gauge, substrate, and clip system, with the lifespan of each option named before fabrication.
Written Estimate and Permitting

A Newark Quality Roofing written estimate sets the scope, labor, materials, and timeline, and the crew files the construction permit a commercial metal roof replacement triggers under N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7 before any work begins.
Tear-Off and Structural Preparation
A Newark Quality Roofing crew removes the existing covering when required, inspects the deck or purlins for structural damage, and completes structural repairs.
Panel Roll-Forming and Installation
A Newark Quality Roofing crew roll-forms standing-seam panels to continuous lengths on site and installs the engineered clip or fastener system, with expansion provisions for runs over 100 feet.
Flashing and Trim Fabrication

A Newark Quality Roofing crew fabricates the ridge caps, valley panels, eave closures, and wall and penetration flashings from matching metal stock and verifies at least ¼ inch per foot of drainage slope, per NRCA and ARMA.
Verification, Cleanup, and Warranty

A Newark Quality Roofing lead verifies panel alignment, seam engagement, and flashing integrity, runs a magnet sweep for fasteners at cleanup, and issues a written workmanship warranty on the labor, separate from the manufacturer material warranty that covers factory defects, per Owens Corning warranty guidance.

sections.heading: Commercial Roof Repair or a New Roof? The 25% Rule for Property Managers

c.v: New Jersey's 25% rule draws the line between commercial roof repair and a permitted project: under N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7, repairing more than 25% of a commercial roof's area in 12 months requires a construction permit, as does any commercial roof replacement.

runs.v: Targeted roof repairs fit leaks at fasteners, seams, and flashing; a new roof fits spreading corrosion, failed seams, or wet insulation and deck rot. Roofing guides commonly estimate that an inspection twice a year can extend roof lifespan by 25 to 50%, and aerial drone inspections help document roof conditions without damage. Inspect fasteners before winter, and avoid aggressive snow removal, which can void metal roof warranties and leave damage that is not covered.

For property managers, the reliability test for a roofing contractor is a professional team with commercial metal expertise, a job-site safety plan, and proof of registration and insurance; New Jersey registers home improvement contractors rather than issuing a separate roofing license, so ask for the registration number instead of accepting "licensed" alone.

faqs.q: How long does a commercial metal roof last?

runs.v: 40 to 80 years: standing-seam metal 40 to 70, exposed-fastener metal about 30 to 50, and copper 70-plus.

faqs.q: What is the difference between standing-seam and exposed-fastener commercial metal roofing?

runs.v: Standing-seam metal conceals the fasteners beneath the raised seam and lasts 40 to 70 years; exposed-fastener metal drives screws through the panel surface at lower cost and lasts about 30 to 50 years.

faqs.q: Should you repair or replace a commercial metal roof?

runs.v: Repair it when damage stays localized; replace it when seam damage passes 25%, panel corrosion passes 20 to 25%, or 15 to 20% of exposed fasteners corrode.

faqs.q: Do you need a permit for a commercial metal roof in Newark, NJ?

runs.v: Yes. A commercial metal roof replacement requires a construction permit under N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7.

faqs.q: How much does commercial metal roofing cost in Essex County, NJ?

runs.v: Commercial metal roofing in New Jersey typically costs $9.00 to $16.00 per square foot installed, and metal repair runs $5 to $10 per square foot.

faqs.q: How does commercial metal roofing handle thermal expansion on long panel runs?

runs.v: Sliding clips let standing-seam panels expand and contract, and runs over 100 feet get engineered expansion provisions, per the Metal Construction Association and the NRCA.

faqs.q: Can a commercial metal roof be installed over an existing roof?

runs.v: Yes, when the existing roof is sound and has fewer than 2 layers; N.J.A.C. 5:23-6.4 requires complete removal when it is water-soaked, is wood, slate, or tile, or already carries 2 or more layers.

faqs.q: What is the biggest problem with metal roofs?

runs.v: Leaks at fasteners, seams, and flashing, as panels expand and contract with each temperature swing and back screws out.

faqs.q: How much does a metal roof cost for a 3,000 sq ft house?

runs.v: Roof area, not floor area, sets the price: at $9.00–$16.00 per square foot installed, 3,000 square feet of roof works out to roughly $27,000–$48,000.
